summary: PC components and parts. eBay is the dominant marketplace — buyers search by exact model number (RTX 3080, Ryzen 7 5800X3D, Samsung 990 PRO, etc.). Generation matters enormously: a current-gen GPU is worth 5-10x its previous generation. Working condition is mandatory; lots described as 'untested' or 'no display' lose 50%+ unless they're a known easy fix (re-paste, BIOS reflash). For estate-auction and shop-cleanout finds, the hidden-gem case is older premium-tier hardware (Noctua coolers, Seasonic PSUs, vintage-tier GPUs) that the seller doesn't know is still desirable.
field_workflow: ALWAYS verify model number on the part itself — boxes alone aren't enough
GPU memory size + bus width are diagnostic (8GB vs 12GB vs 16GB drives price)
Power Supply: check 80+ rating (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum/Titanium) and total wattage
RAM: speed (MHz) + capacity (8/16/32/64GB) + DDR generation are all part of the search
SSD: model number on label tells generation (PCIe Gen3/4/5) — major price differential
HDD: SMART data history if available; bad sectors kill resale
Working / tested status doubles value — 'powered on, no further testing' is the worst middle ground
skip_list: OEM bulk pull-from-Dell / pull-from-HP (these are mass-produced and don't comp well)
Counterfeit RAM (always test in a known-good system)
Pre-2000 PC hardware (mostly e-waste unless retro-collector category)
GPU with bent fins / missing fans

era_markers: Model number etched on heat spreader (e.g. 100-000000059)
Box with Wraith Stealth/Spire/Prism cooler (premium for AMD-included cooler)
Original retail packaging vs OEM tray
Production date code on bottom of CPU
brands.notes: X3D variants are the gaming sweet spot — premium over base models. Always run AIDA64 / Cinebench / OCCT to verify stability before listing.

era_markers: Generation prefix on model (4th/6th/7th/8th/9th/10th/11th/12th/13th/14th gen)
K suffix (overclockable) vs F suffix (no iGPU) vs T (low-power)
S-Spec (SR-prefix) etched on heat spreader — buyers grep for it
Xeon socket: LGA2011-3 (E5 v3/v4) / LGA3647 (Gold/Silver/Platinum)
13th/14th gen K-series affected by oxidation/degradation issue (deduct value)
brands.notes: Volume movers from eBay sold-research are the older mainstream Intel desktop CPUs (i5-6500 → i5-12600 spread) and decommissioned-data-center Xeons. T-suffix variants fit Mini/SFF builds and command a slight premium. Always include the S-Spec (SRxxx) on listings — buyers filter by it. 13th/14th gen K-series have a known degradation issue.

era_markers: ASUS branding with ROG / TUF / Prime line label
Original packaging with model SKU sticker
GPU PCB etched ASUS marking
Motherboard chipset (Z690/B550/X670/B760 etc.)
brands.notes: ROG Strix / Maximus are the premium tiers — 20-30% premium over TUF / Prime equivalents. Check fans on GPUs (sagging or bent = deduct), and that motherboard pins are straight (bent CPU socket pins kill resale).

era_markers: MSI branding with Gaming X / Suprim / Ventus tier
Original packaging with hologram seal
GPU PCB MSI marking
Motherboard MEG / MPG / MAG / PRO designation
brands.notes: Suprim is MSI's flagship (above Gaming X). Tomahawk is the mainstream-favorite mobo line. Check for backplate dents and verify display output works before listing.

era_markers: Gigabyte branding with AORUS premium label
Aurora-orange / falcon graphic for AORUS
Original packaging with model SKU
Vision (creator-line) light cream colorway
brands.notes: AORUS is Gigabyte's premium tier — Master/Xtreme top-out the line. Vision is the white/cream creator line, hot for content creators with white-themed builds.

era_markers: ASRock branding with line label (Taichi / Phantom / Steel Legend)
Original retail packaging
Chipset model marked on board
brands.notes: ASRock Taichi has loyal following for VRM quality and feature density. Mini-ITX boards from any maker premium over standard ATX (small form-factor builds are hot).

era_markers: Zotac branding with AMP / Trinity / Twin Edge tier
Original packaging
5-year warranty registration card (transferable)
brands.notes: Zotac runs cooler/quieter than some competitors but commands slightly less premium. The 5-year warranty (registered) is transferable and adds value.

era_markers: EVGA branding with FTW3 / KINGPIN / XC3 line
EVGA stopped making GPUs in 2022 — older RTX 30xx EVGA cards are last-of-line collectibles
EVGA PSU 80+ rating (Gold/Platinum/Titanium) on label
Made in Taiwan stamping
brands.notes: EVGA exited the GPU market in 2022 — last-generation EVGA RTX 30-series cards are now end-of-line and sit at premium pricing as collectibles. Their PSUs (especially SuperNOVA G+ and Titanium-rated) are still available and trade well.

era_markers: PNY branding with XLR8 / VERTO line label
PCIe Gen3 vs Gen4 vs Gen5 marked on SSD label
Capacity sticker (1TB / 2TB / 4TB / 8TB)
brands.notes: Volume play — PNY GPUs trade slightly below premium-tier (ASUS/MSI/Gigabyte) at the same NVIDIA SKU. Their SSDs are mid-tier value but reliable. Quadro Pro line (workstation GPUs) commands much higher than gaming.

era_markers: Sapphire Toxic = top-tier (premium over Nitro+)
Vapor-X chamber cooling marked on label (premium signal)
Original packaging often blue/silver Sapphire colorway
Backplate logo style varies by model gen
brands.notes: Sapphire is the most-respected AMD board partner — Toxic and Nitro+ command premium even over MSI/ASUS Radeon equivalents. Limited Edition / Anniversary models are collector premium.

era_markers: XFX with Speedster series label
MERC = top-tier, QICK = mid, SWFT = entry
Triple-fan vs dual-fan visible from photo
Original retail box
brands.notes: XFX MERC line offers excellent thermals at mid-tier prices. Their double-warranty registration program adds resale value when transferred.

era_markers: PowerColor with Red Devil / Liquid Devil flagship
Hellhound is the mid-tier sweet spot
Limited Edition releases (Red Devil LE) are scarce-numbered
Liquid Devil = AIO water-cooled (collectible)
brands.notes: Red Devil Limited Editions are numbered runs and trade at collector premium. Liquid Devil (AIO water-cooled) versions command 30-50% premium over air-cooled equivalents.

era_markers: Corsair branding with line label (Vengeance / RM / iCUE)
80+ certification on PSU label (Gold/Platinum/Titanium)
Wattage and modular/non-modular status visible
RAM speed (3200/3600/6000/7200 MT/s) on heat-spreader sticker
DDR4 vs DDR5 marked on package
brands.notes: Corsair spans RAM, PSUs, cases, and AIO coolers — verify which product before listing. AX series PSUs (Platinum/Titanium) hold value well. RGB lighting working = factor (broken RGB = -30%).

era_markers: G.Skill branding with Trident / Ripjaws line
Speed (MT/s) and CL timings on heat-spreader sticker
Royal series has crystalline diffuser top (collectible)
DDR4 (Z / Z RGB) vs DDR5 (Z5 / Z5 RGB)
brands.notes: Trident Z Royal is the showpiece tier (mirror finish + crystalline LEDs). Z5 (DDR5) at 6000-7200 MT/s is the current sweet spot for AM5/Intel 12-14th gen builds. Test in a known-good system before listing — counterfeits exist.

era_markers: Crucial branding (subsidiary of Micron)
DDR4 vs DDR5 marked on package
PCIe Gen3 (P3) / Gen4 (P5/P5 Plus) / Gen5 (T700/T705) on SSD label
Capacity (1TB / 2TB / 4TB) on label
brands.notes: T705 is the fastest consumer NVMe currently. MX500 is the long-running SATA budget favorite. RAM tier is mid (Pro line) — for premium, look at G.Skill or Corsair Dominator.

era_markers: Kingston branding with Fury line label
Speed (MT/s) and timings on heat-spreader
PCIe Gen3 (NV2) / Gen4 (KC3000 / NV3 / Renegade)
Made in USA / Taiwan / Mexico stamps
brands.notes: Fury Renegade is Kingston's enthusiast tier (RAM + SSD). KC3000 was the standout NVMe of its generation. Avoid generic Kingston DDR3 / SATA — commodity-tier resale.

era_markers: T-Force / TeamGroup with line designation
Speed and CL timings on RAM
PCIe Gen4 vs Gen5 on SSD label
Original packaging w/ hologram
brands.notes: TeamGroup is value-tier with enthusiast performance. T-Force Vulcan / Delta RGB are the consumer flagships. Quietly excellent for budget-conscious builders — don't write off as no-name.

era_markers: Samsung branding with model number (980 / 990 / 970 etc.)
PRO = top-tier, EVO = mainstream, QVO = budget (QLC)
PCIe Gen3 (970) / Gen4 (980/990) / Gen5 (future)
T-series = portable, on USB cable
brands.notes: Samsung 990 PRO + 980 PRO are reference-tier NVMe drives. Counterfeits exist — verify model number on label and run CrystalDiskMark / Samsung Magician health check before listing. T7 Shield's rugged housing commands premium over plain T7.

era_markers: Western Digital / WD branding with color line
Black = NVMe gaming / Blue = mainstream / Red = NAS / Purple = surveillance / Gold = enterprise
Capacity stamped on shell (TB rating)
CMR vs SMR designation on Red Plus / Red

comp_ranges_usd.item: WD Red Plus 8TB CMR NAS HDD

brands.notes: Easystore / Elements externals are commonly 'shucked' for the WD Red CMR drive inside — this is a major hobby and large-capacity examples (12-22TB) trade close to bare-drive prices. WD Gold / Ultrastar enterprise drives have data-center buyer pool.

era_markers: Seagate branding with line label (IronWolf / Exos / BarraCuda)
Capacity stamped (8TB / 16TB / 18TB / 20TB / 22TB)
Pro suffix = higher MTBF / longer warranty
Original retail box vs OEM bare drive
brands.notes: Exos enterprise drives (16-22TB) are the volume play — recertified or new-pull lots trade well to homelab buyers. Always run SMART check before listing — Seagate has had reliability scrutiny periodically.

era_markers: Toshiba branding with model series
MG / N300 / P300 line designations (enterprise / NAS / consumer)
Capacity stamped
brands.notes: Toshiba is the third-place HDD maker after WD/Seagate but their enterprise MG-series competes well on $/TB. Lower brand recognition = sometimes-better deals at auction.

era_markers: Sabrent branding with Rocket model line
Rocket 4 Plus = PCIe Gen4 (consumer flagship)
Rocket 5 = PCIe Gen5 (top-end)
Capacity on label (1TB / 2TB / 4TB / 8TB)
brands.notes: Sabrent Rocket 4 Plus 8TB is one of the few consumer NVMe drives at that capacity — strong demand from creators who need single-volume large NVMe. Rocket 5 is bleeding-edge Gen5.

era_markers: Seasonic branding with PRIME / FOCUS / VERTEX series
80+ rating (Gold / Platinum / Titanium)
Wattage on label (650W / 850W / 1000W / 1300W / 1600W)
PRIME Titanium = highest tier
Made in Taiwan stamping
brands.notes: Seasonic OEMs PSUs for Corsair AX/RM, EVGA SuperNOVA G+, NZXT C series, and others — when you see one branded Corsair AXi or EVGA G7, it's actually Seasonic internally. Their own-brand PRIME line is the gold standard.

era_markers: be quiet! branding (lowercase, with exclamation mark)
Dark Power Pro = top-tier PSU
Dark Rock Pro = top-tier air cooler
Made in Germany stamping (older)
brands.notes: be quiet! is the silent-build favorite — Dark Power Pro PSUs and Dark Rock Pro air coolers have dedicated silent-build buyers. Premium German engineering; often 20-30% above Corsair equivalents.

era_markers: Fractal Design branding (Sweden)
Tempered glass side vs solid (premium silent vs visible)
Original retail box
North series wood front panel (collectible)
brands.notes: North series is iconic for warm-wood aesthetic — strong appeal to creator/photographer demographics. Define 7 and Meshify 2 are workhorse premium ATX cases. Note: cases are heavy and hard to ship — only worth it if margin justifies the large_box freight.

era_markers: Lian Li branding (Taiwan)
Dual-chamber layout (O11 series signature)
Aluminum panels on premium models
Original packaging w/ accessory baggies
brands.notes: Lian Li O11 Dynamic IS the showcase-build case — every modder/streamer running RGB has one. Strong resale even years after original release. SFX (small form factor) cases like DAN A4 trade premium because Lian Li discontinues runs frequently.

era_markers: NZXT branding with H-series number
Flow / Elite suffix indicates airflow vs glass-window variant
H1 ITX has integrated PSU/cooler (collectible)
Older Phantom / Source series = legacy
brands.notes: NZXT H1 (compact ITX with built-in PSU/cooler) had a recall but the redesigned version is sought-after. Kraken Z (with LCD display) commands big premium over X (no display).

era_markers: Cooler Master branding with Master/HAF/Cosmos line
HAF series = high-airflow flagship line
Cosmos = top-tier showcase case
NR200 / NR200P = popular SFF-ITX
brands.notes: NR200 / NR200P is the dominant ITX case at its price point — discontinued runs trade close to retail. Cosmos C700M and HAF 700 EVO are showpiece flagships. Older HAF (922/X) has a vintage-modder following.

era_markers: Noctua branding (Austria) with brown-on-cream colorway
chromax.black = all-black variant (premium)
NF-A12x25 = reference 120mm fan (industry standard)
Made in Taiwan stamping
brands.notes: Noctua holds value better than ANY other PC component — the brown/cream color is iconic and the NF-A12x25 fan IS the industry-reference 120mm. chromax.black variants are limited stock and trade close to MSRP even years after release.

era_markers: Thermalright branding (Taiwan)
SE suffix = Special Edition (premium variant)
Original packaging with mounting hardware accessories
Le Grand Macho = legacy cult favorite
brands.notes: Peerless Assassin 120 is the budget-king dual-tower air cooler — disrupted Noctua's price tier. Quietly excellent value. Le Grand Macho has a vintage-cooler cult following.

era_markers: Arctic branding (Switzerland-designed, Taiwan-made)
Liquid Freezer II/III = AIO water cooler line
Freezer 34/36 eSports = air cooler line
P12/P14 fans are popular with budget builders
brands.notes: Arctic Liquid Freezer III is the consensus budget AIO champion — punches up at Corsair / NZXT pricing. P12/P14 fans are mass-market favorites. Don't confuse with Arctic Silver thermal paste.

era_markers: Tesla branding with model code (V100/P100/P40/P4/T4/A100 etc.)
SXM2 = mezzanine connector (needs server backplane); PCIe = standard slot
Memory size + type: HBM2 (V100/P100/A100), GDDR5 (P40), GDDR6 (T4)
NVIDIA part number 699-XXXXX-XXXX-XXX on board PCB
Half-height passive cooler (no fan) typical — server-only thermal
Half-rack form factor with mounting brackets
brands.notes: MASSIVE volume movers from eBay sold-research. P100 16GB had 5+ separate listings each clearing 60-200 units in 30 days. P40 24GB is the LLM/AI-hobbyist favorite (24GB VRAM at low price). V100 SXM2 form-factor needs a special HGX/server backplane to use — many buyers don't realize this; includes SXM2 in title to set expectations. PCIe-form variants are plug-and-play. Always verify the part number sticker (699-XXXXX) and disclose air-cooled vs passive (passive = needs forced-air rack chassis).

era_markers: Quadro branding (older) → RTX A-series (current Ampere) → RTX Ada (current generation)
Memory size in GB stamped on heatsink
Half-height (single-slot) bracket on lower-tier cards
Standard PCIe form factor — works in any desktop
brands.notes: Workstation GPUs (CAD / 3D rendering / video editing). RTX A-series is the current pro line; older Quadro K/M/P series come from corporate refurb / CAD-shop cleanouts. Memory size matters more than core count for the workstation buyer pool. PNY is the OEM partner (PNY NVIDIA branding common). Verify display outputs work — DisplayPort connector lifecycle is shorter than the GPU silicon.

era_markers: Radeon Pro / FirePro / Instinct branding (server vs workstation lines)
AMD part number 102-XXXXXX-XX on PCB
Server cards typically passive cooled (no fan) — need server chassis airflow
Workstation cards (W-series, WX-series) have active fans
brands.notes: AMD's server/workstation GPU line — much smaller volume than NVIDIA Tesla but the V620 32GB had 59 units sold in 30 days at ~$380. Radeon Pro WX (workstation) and Instinct (server) both have CAD/scientific buyer pools. Many include 'Read Description' suffix — they're often missing display outputs or have OEM-locked firmware. Verify before bidding aggressively.

era_markers: CMP HX = NVIDIA's purpose-built mining card (no display outputs)
P102/P104/P106 = compute-only Pascal mining variants (mid-2010s)
Hashrate often listed in title (e.g., 20-24 MH/s for RVN)
No display outputs on most — confirms mining-only
brands.notes: Crypto-mining GPUs. CMP HX line is NVIDIA's officially-sanctioned mining cards (no display outputs, locked driver). P102/P104/P106 are pre-CMP Pascal mining variants with same architecture as GTX 1080 Ti / 1070 Ti. Useful for AI inference at low VRAM thresholds. Disclose mining history in listings — buyers expect post-mining wear (high hours, fan + thermal-paste replacement common).

era_markers: Radeon RX / R9 / HD branding with model number
Memory size + bus width on heatsink/bracket
Brand sub-line (Sapphire Pulse / Nitro+ / XFX RS / etc.) on PCB
DVI / DisplayPort / HDMI output mix tells the gen
brands.notes: Older AMD consumer GPUs — strong volume from estate-sale and shop-cleanout lots. Sapphire Pulse RX 5700 XT 8GB was a $150 volume mover. RX 580/590 8GB cards have a budget-gaming buyer pool. Note: many of these are post-mining cards (RX 470/480/570/580 era was big mining demand) — disclose if known.

era_markers: GTX (no RTX cores) = pre-2018; RTX = 2018+ (Turing onwards)
Memory size + GDDR generation on heatsink shroud
Brand sub-line (FTW3 / Gaming X / ROG Strix / etc.) visible
Display output mix tells the gen (DVI fading after RTX 30-series)

comp_ranges_usd.item: GTX 980 / 980 Ti (volume mover at low price)

brands.notes: Older NVIDIA consumer GPUs from estate-sale + shop-cleanout. GTX 980 G1 Gaming at $38 had 43 units in 30 days — volume play. RTX 2080 Ti remains a cult chip (chunky 11GB, decent for ML even today). GTX 1080 Ti has nostalgic premium. Card brand (EVGA FTW3 / ROG Strix / Gaming X) ALSO matters — premium tiers add 20-40%.

era_markers: 12VHPWR = ATX 3.0 / PCIe 5.0 connector (newer; RTX 4080/4090/5080/5090)
8-pin / 6+2 pin = legacy PCIe power (everything pre-RTX 40-series)
Connector counts on each end visible from photo
Color-coded brand cables (EVGA red, Corsair black, etc.) for modular PSUs
brands.notes: Surprisingly steady volume from eBay sold-research — 12VHPWR adapter at $8 had 188 units in 30 days. The RTX 40/50-series adoption created sustained demand for these cables. Cheap individual price means they only matter as multi-pack BOLO targets.

era_markers: Mini-ITX form factor (170 × 170 mm) — distinctive small square PCB
Embedded SoC variants (Celeron J / Atom N) have CPU soldered on
Standard Mini-ITX (LGA1200/1700/AM4/AM5) have a real socket
I/O shield often included with retail packaging
brands.notes: Mini-ITX commands premium per-square-inch — small-form-factor builders pay up. The Gigabyte GA-J1900N-D3V (Celeron embedded) had 70 units in 30 days at $26 — used by NAS / pfSense / Proxmox builders for low-power 24/7 servers. Always confirm CPU socket type and chipset in title.

era_markers: Raspberry Pi Foundation logo on PCB
Model number stamped on board (e.g. Raspberry Pi 4 Model B)
RAM size variant — Pi 4 comes in 1GB / 2GB / 4GB / 8GB
Pi 5 has dual-CSI / dual-DSI connector (vs Pi 4)
Pico / Pico W = RP2040 microcontroller (different product)

comp_ranges_usd.item: Raspberry Pi 3 Model B / B+ (volume mover)

brands.notes: Pi 3 Model B was the #1 and #2 best-seller in the past 30 days of CPU-category eBay sold-listings. Massive volume across all generations because of education + IoT + retro-gaming demand. Include RAM size for Pi 4 (4GB/8GB) — that's the price-driving spec. Verify the SoC sticker isn't peeled off (counterfeit/refurb signal).

era_markers: Intel NUC branding with model number on bottom
FNH suffix = standard 'tall' chassis (room for 2.5" SSD)
FNK suffix = 'short' chassis (M.2 only)
Canyon codenames (Hades / Ghost / Beast / Dragon) = enthusiast/gaming NUCs
Pro suffix = business/embedded line
brands.notes: Intel discontinued NUC in 2023 (now ASUS NUC) — older NUCs increasingly behave as collectibles. Hades/Ghost/Beast Canyon enthusiast NUCs hold value strongest. Volume mover from the eBay research is NUC10i3FNH at ~$95. Always specify whether barebone (no RAM/SSD) or fully populated.

era_markers: Form factor designation: SFF (Small Form Factor) / DM (Desktop Mini) / Micro / Tiny
Generation digit (G3/G4/G5/G6 for HP, last digit on Dell OptiPlex)
CPU is usually a -T suffix variant (low-power desktop)
Power brick (external PSU) often missing — check listing photos

comp_ranges_usd.item: HP ProDesk 600 G4 DM with i5-8500T (volume mover)
HP EliteDesk 800 G5 / G6 with i7-T
Lenovo ThinkCentre M90q Tiny with i5/i7
Older G3 / 5050 / M715q without OS or SSD

brands.notes: Off-lease corporate refurbs — massive supply, steady demand from homelab / Plex / pfSense / Proxmox builders. Power brick + presence of SSD/RAM both major price drivers. The HP ProDesk 600 G4 DM with i5-8500T at ~$70 was the volume mover from the eBay research.

era_markers: Brand label visible on syringe / tube
Net weight stamped (1g / 2g / 4g / 6g / 20g typical)
Original sealed packaging vs opened (opened = lower value)
Multi-pack listings (5-pack / 6-pack syringes) are popular volume movers
brands.notes: Surprisingly high-volume category from the eBay research (Arctic MX-6 hit 193 units sold in 30 days). Generic 'silver/gold thermal grease' syringes also move steadily as multi-packs. Tiny ship class — fits in a poly mailer. Avoid expired / dried-out tubes (factory-sealed only).

era_markers: HP DPS-XXXXAB or DPS-XXXXRB on PSU label (made by Delta)
HP / HSTNS-PD prefix part number visible on case
Workstation Z-series labels (Z240/Z440/Z640/Z840) on chassis-fit PSUs
80+ rating sticker (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum) when consumer-grade
Proprietary form factor — fits ONLY HP chassis of the listed series
brands.notes: Massive volume from corporate-refurb wholesalers. HP DPS-750RB at $20 had 60 units in 30 days. Workstation PSUs (Z440/Z840 etc.) are PROPRIETARY form factors — they only fit the matching HP chassis. Buyers searching for OptiPlex/ProDesk/Envy replacements are highly motivated. Always include the HP part number (700-something or L-prefix) and the chassis it fits in the title.

era_markers: Dell on white chassis label, with H/L-prefix model number
Dell part number (alphanumeric e.g. H240AS-00, 2XK8W)
PowerEdge R-series = rack server; T-series = tower; precision = workstation
Proprietary form factor — only fits the Dell chassis listed
brands.notes: Steady corporate-refurb volume. The Dell '240w 360w 500w' multi-fit PSU at $75 had 8 units in 30 days. PowerEdge server PSUs are the rack-server homelab-buyer staple. OptiPlex SFF PSUs are proprietary — buyers replacing dead PSUs in Dell SFF business desktops are a fixed audience. Include the chassis model AND the Dell part number (H240AS-00 etc.) for searchability.

era_markers: SuperMicro on PSU label with PWS-prefix part number
Wattage stamped (200W / 800W / 1200W / 2000W / 3000W)
80+ rating (Gold / Platinum / Titanium) on label
1U / 2U / 4U form-factor designation
Hot-swap module form (with rear connector finger)
brands.notes: SuperMicro PSUs are server-only modules — fit specific 1U/2U/4U Supermicro chassis. Buyer pool is data-center decommission resellers and homelab builders running used Supermicro servers. Titanium-rated units (PWS-3K06G) trade at strong premium. Disclose hot-swap chassis fit clearly.

era_markers: Brand on label (MSI / Gigabyte / Cooler Master / Thermaltake / Super Flower / Segotep / FSP)
Wattage stamped (450W-1600W)
80+ rating (Bronze / Silver / Gold / Platinum / Titanium)
Modular / Semi-modular / Non-modular designation
ATX 3.0 / PCIe 5.0 / 12VHPWR connector for newer units
Original cables included or absent (-30% if missing)

comp_ranges_usd.item: Gigabyte AORUS P1000W / Gigabyte GP-P850GM Gold
MSI MAG A750GL Gold modular (volume mover)

brands.notes: Mid-tier consumer PSUs — below Corsair RM/HX or EVGA SuperNOVA G+ but above generic Chinese builds. MSI MAG A750GL was a $60 / 48-unit volume mover. Super Flower Leadex Titanium retains value strongly. Segotep is the budget tier (Chinese OEM with 80+ Gold cert). FSP both makes their own consumer PSUs AND OEM's for proprietary HP/Lenovo PSUs.

era_markers: Apple branding on PSU label
Apple part number 614-XXXX or 661-XXXXX
Mac chassis model (A1186 / A1289 / A1419 / A1407 etc.)
Wattage (185W / 305W / 760W / 980W / 1300W typical)
Made for specific Mac year — not interchangeable across generations
brands.notes: Legacy Apple repair-parts market. iMac PSUs are a steady-volume repair part because thermal cycling kills them but the rest of the iMac is still useful. Mac Pro 1,1 980W PSU is the cult-classic repair part for vintage cheese-grater Mac Pros. Always disclose chassis fitment by year/model — Apple PSUs are not cross-compatible.

era_markers: Brand stamp on cold-plate / radiator side-tank / reservoir
Material specified (copper / brass / acrylic / acetal)
Size: 120mm / 140mm / 240mm / 280mm / 360mm / 420mm / 480mm radiator
Thread spec G1/4 (universal) on fittings
Pump model (D5 / DDC / VPP755) on reservoir+pump combos
Lighting: D-RGB / A-RGB / aRGB / RGB Fusion compatibility

comp_ranges_usd.item: EKWB EK-Quantum Velocity / Magnitude CPU block
Hardware Labs Black Ice Nemesis 280 GTS

brands.notes: Premium custom-loop water cooling brands. EKWB, Alphacool, XSPC, Hardware Labs, Bitspower are the enthusiast-tier brands — buyers know exact model numbers. NZXT Kraken / Lian Li Galahad / DeepCool LT-series are the top-tier closed-loop AIOs. Lots tagged 'used untested' lose 40-50%; 'tested working with screenshots' command full retail. Custom-loop part bundles (mixed reservoirs + radiator + pump) often go for less than sum-of-parts at auction — good profit if patient.

brands.brand: Budget water cooling parts (FreezeMod / Barrow / etc.)
era_markers: Brand stamp (FreezeMod / Barrow / Bykski / OCOCOO / Dracaena / OCOOL)
G1/4 thread is universal — fitting brand mostly cosmetic
Tubing OD/ID specified (10/13mm, 12/16mm, 16mm OD hard)
Radiator length stamped (120/240/280/360/420/480mm)
Material called out (all copper / aluminum / brass)
Thickness for radiators (28/30/45/65mm) — premium signal
brands.notes: Budget Chinese-OEM water cooling brands. FreezeMod is the dominant budget radiator + pump volume mover (15+ listings in 30 days). Barrow is the fittings + tubing leader. Bykski makes mid-tier blocks. These compete on price not brand prestige — buyers cross-shop on G1/4 thread compatibility (universal). Estate-sale finds in custom-loop builders' garage cleanouts often have $400+ in mixed parts.

era_markers: Server / enterprise OEM PCB-stamped fan label
Vendor-specific part number (Dell 2ND0R, HPE p48908-b21, etc.)
Hot-swap module form factor (rear handle / latch)
Proprietary connector (mini-fit / 6-pin / 8-pin) NOT standard 4-pin PWM
Air-flow direction marking (Front-to-Rear / Rear-to-Front / AFO)

era_markers: Pico-PSU = palm-sized 12V module with bare board PCB
Flex ATX = 1U / Mini-ITX form factor PSU (longer than SFX, not as tall)
Breakout board = adapter to convert server PSU rails to GPU 6+2 cables
Mining kit = bundle of server PSU + breakout + GPU cables
brands.notes: Niche but consistent buyers. Pico PSUs for tiny SFF / car-PC / digital signage builds. Flex ATX 1U server PSUs for industrial/embedded use. Mining breakout boards repurpose surplus server PSUs (HP 1200W from 2010s) for mining rigs — strong nostalgia segment.

platform_notes.eBay: Dominant marketplace for PC parts — buyers search by exact model number and convert at high rates. Use sold-listings filter (LH_Sold=1&LH_Complete=1) for accurate comps.
platform_notes.r/hardwareswap (Reddit): Active community for clean used parts — verify with seller's flair / comment history. Not a place to ship stock from but useful for sanity-checking comps.
platform_notes.Newegg / Best Buy refurb: These set the floor for refurbished prices. eBay used sells at 70-85% of refurb MSRP.
